answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a single vertex in a shared reputation graph, where the vertex gains weight only through attested work for real counterparties. A new identity enters through one narrow inlet: it must lock a refundable bond and complete verified tasks before transacting at full value. A flood of cheap fakes then faces a frozen tundra — each sock puppet needs its own bond and its own slow trust climb, so creating a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds, while honest agents keep one cheap, well-connected vertex.
